prime.problem: You can't load OpenAI's GPT-2 weights, or train your own copy, until you have a PyTorch model with exactly the right pieces, the right shapes and the right names. One misnamed or misshapen module and the 149 checkpoint tensors have nowhere to go.
prime.fits: z2h-8 built a small GPT for Shakespeare. This card rewrites that same architecture at GPT-2's size and in GPT-2's arrangement (pre-norm, final ln_f, tanh-GELU), with names that match the checkpoint you toured on the target card.
expect: the residual stream x of shape (B, T, 768)
attention as a reduce, the MLP as a map
prime.goal: Write GPT, Block and MLP from memory, explain why each Block adds to the stream instead of replacing it, and account for all 124,439,808 parameters by hand.

attend: Where exactly does the LayerNorm sit in a GPT-2 Block, and what stays on the plain x → x path because of that placement?
Which sublayer lets token 5 use information from token 2, and which one never mixes positions?
Why does c_attn output 2304 numbers per token rather than 768?
How does the Python attribute path self.transformer['h'][0].attn turn into the key transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.weight?
Which part of the 124M model grows with depth (n_layer) and which grows only with the vocabulary?

must: Each Block computes x + f(ln(x)) → the Block adds a correction instead of replacing x → an untouched identity path runs from the embeddings to ln_f → signals and gradients reach the bottom of a 12-Block stack without passing through 24 LayerNorms in series (the post-norm problem)

Attention mixes information across positions (reduce) while the MLP transforms each token alone (map) → alternating them 12 times lets tokens gather context, then process it → the MLP's 4× widening (768 → 3072 → 768) makes it hold about 2/3 of every Block's parameters

PyTorch names parameters by attribute path → using OpenAI's names (transformer.wte, h, attn.c_attn, ln_f, lm_head) makes our state_dict keys equal the checkpoint's → loading becomes a loop over matching keys, and a naming slip shows up as a missing key instead of a silently wrong model

Parameters per Block ≈ 12·C² (c_attn 3C², attn c_proj C², c_fc 4C², mlp c_proj 4C²) → 12 Blocks × 7.09M = 85.1M, 68% of the model → the one 50257 × 768 token table is most of the rest (31%), which is why tying it matters
elevated: nn.GELU(approximate='tanh') instead of the exact GELU → the two differ by at most 0.000473 on [−5, 5] → irrelevant for a fresh model, but needed to reproduce OpenAI's weights exactly

nn.ModuleList (not a plain Python list) for h → PyTorch registers each Block's parameters → they appear in parameters() and state_dict() as h.0 … h.11; a plain list would hide them from the optimizer and from loading
reference: the exact GPTConfig fields and defaults (block_size 1024, vocab_size 50257, n_layer 12, n_head 12, n_embd 768)
per-module counts: c_attn 1,771,776 · attn c_proj 590,592 · c_fc 2,362,368 · mlp c_proj 2,360,064 · 2 LayerNorms 3,072

compress.prompt: From memory, draw GPT-2 from token ids to logits, with shapes on every arrow, and write the two lines of Block.forward. Then explain in 3–4 sentences why the Block is written as x = x + ….
checklist: idx (B, T) → wte + wpe → x (B, T, 768) → 12 Blocks → ln_f → lm_head → logits (B, T, 50257)
x = x + attn(ln_1(x)) then x = x + mlp(ln_2(x)): LayerNorm before each branch (pre-norm)
the residual add keeps a clean path for signal and gradient through all 12 Blocks
attention = tokens exchange information; MLP = each token processed alone
names match the HF checkpoint so weights load key by key

retrieve.q: Explain what the residual stream is in GPT-2 and why every Block adds to it rather than overwriting it.
answer: a (B, T, 768) tensor carried from the embeddings to ln_f
each branch computes a correction from a normalised copy and adds it back
the plain identity path lets gradients reach early Blocks and the embeddings directly

retrieve.q: Walk one token's 768-vector through a single Block: which modules touch it, in what order, and what shape comes out of each?
answer: ln_1 → 768; c_attn → 2304 (q, k, v, each 12 heads × 64); attention mixes with earlier tokens → 768; c_proj → 768; added to x
ln_2 → 768; c_fc → 3072; tanh-GELU → 3072; c_proj → 768; added to x
output is (B, T, 768), the same shape as the input, so Blocks stack

retrieve.q: You want a bigger model for the same memory. Adding Blocks and widening n_embd both add parameters: how does each scale, and what do you give up if you choose depth?
answer: each Block costs about 12·C² (7,087,872 at C = 768), so depth adds linearly
width grows the Block cost as C² and the token table as 50257·C
more Blocks means more sequential steps per forward pass, and deeper stacks lean harder on the residual path and on init (the init card)

retrieve.q: Your state_dict has a key transformer.blocks.0.attn.c_attn.weight while the checkpoint has transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.weight. What went wrong in your class, and what does the loader see?
answer: the ModuleList was assigned to blocks instead of h
keys are built from attribute names, so all 12 Blocks' keys differ
a key-matching loader finds them missing, or a non-strict load leaves those weights random

compare.q: z2h-8's nanoGPT and this GPT-2 module compute nearly the same thing. What is fundamentally the same, which differences come from matching OpenAI's checkpoint, and when would you keep z2h-8's choices?
answer: same: embeddings + positions, pre-norm Blocks with attention and MLP, final LayerNorm, a linear head
GPT-2 specific: HF names, tanh-GELU, 50,257-token BPE vocab, 1024 context, no dropout in build-nanogpt, tied head
keep z2h-8's naming and dropout for a small model trained from scratch on a small dataset where overfitting is the risk
failure modes: z2h-8's names can't load OpenAI weights; skipping dropout can overfit a small dataset

compare.q: This card builds the empty shell; the next fills it with OpenAI's numbers. What does loading rely on from this card, and what still differs even when every name matches?
answer: loading relies on identical key names and identical shapes per key
four weights (c_attn, attn c_proj, c_fc, mlp c_proj) are stored transposed in OpenAI's Conv1D layout and must be flipped
a wrong name gives a missing key; a wrong orientation gives a shape mismatch or garbage logits

predict.q: Build GPT(GPTConfig(n_layer=1)): one Block instead of twelve. Before running it, estimate the parameter count and what share of it is the token table wte.
predict.answer: 46,473,216 parameters (measured for this card), of which wte is 38,597,376 = 83%. Removing 11 Blocks removes 11 × 7,087,872 = 77,966,592 parameters, but the vocabulary table doesn't shrink with depth. Small models are dominated by their embedding table, which is why weight tying matters most at small sizes.

apply.task: Write a function count(L, C, V=50257, T=1024) that predicts the parameter count from the per-module shapes on this card (with wte tied to lm_head). Check it against GPT(GPTConfig()), then predict GPT-2 medium (n_layer 24, n_head 16, n_embd 1024) before building it.
apply.done: Your formula gives 124,439,808 for the 124M config and 354,823,168 for medium, and sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) agrees on both (both measured for this card).
apply.hint: One Block is 12·C² + 13·C: four weight matrices totalling 12·C², plus biases 3C + C + 4C + C and two LayerNorms of 2C each. Add V·C + T·C + 2C for wte, wpe and ln_f.

reflect: Which prediction did you get wrong: attention vs MLP size, or how much of a 1-Block model is the token table?
What couldn't you explain cleanly about why pre-norm keeps a clean residual path?
Which relationship is still fuzzy: attribute names → state_dict keys, or state_dict keys → loading OpenAI's weights?
If you had to change one thing in GPTConfig to double the model, which would you pick, and why?
What from z2h-8 did you have to unlearn (names, dropout, activation) to write this version?
